claims.text: The initial eutectic high-entropy-alloy microstructure consists of dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries.
Controlled solidification and thermomechanical processing can produce lamellar colony sizes of 10–50 μm.
Controlled solidification and thermomechanical processing can produce a preferred lamellar orientation.
Refining lamellar colony size reduces microcracking during room-temperature tensile deformation.
Optimizing lamellar orientation reduces microcracking during room-temperature tensile deformation.
Refined colony size and optimized lamellar orientation improve strain accommodation.
Reduced microcracking and improved strain accommodation increase yield strength.
Reduced microcracking and improved strain accommodation increase room-temperature tensile ductility.
The optimized microstructure will increase yield strength by 20% relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline.
The optimized microstructure will increase tensile elongation by 30% relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline.
The proposed beneficial regime requires a lamellar colony size between 10 and 50 μm and an orientation deviation within 10°.
The magnitude of the strength and ductility improvements depends on alloy composition and processing conditions.

contradictions.description: The stated prediction is a 20% yield-strength increase and a 30% elongation increase, but the hypothesis is only falsified below 10% and 20%, respectively. Outcomes between those values would fail the quantitative prediction without satisfying the stated falsification rule.
